tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The compliance sampler intake sat in a shallow corner of the effluent channel where wind piled floating debris.
In house samples were drawn from the well mixed centre of the same channel.
A paired sampling day showed corner samples three times the centre TSS, with visible debris in the corner bottles.
Moving the intake to the mixed zone in a trial brought compliance and in house results into agreement on the next windy day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The compliance sampler intake location collects wind piled debris and overstates effluent TSS
The plant truly loses solids on windy days and in house sampling misses it
The compliance laboratory over reads TSS
Wind resuspends the clarifier blanket on those days

inference.explanation: Clarifier blanket was normal, the compliance lab passed its checks, and paired sampling plus the intake move isolate location.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Compliance lab quality control record
Clarifier blanket trend on windy days
Paired corner versus centre sampling record paired with the intake relocation trial

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The compliance lab checks were in range.
clueText.nc-b: Blanket stayed normal on the windy days.
clueText.nc-c: Compliance results match in house results once the intake sits in mixed flow.

tasks.prompt: A pH loop kept dosing alkali in bursts, and basin pH swung between 6.2 and 7.8 each day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The pH electrode response in buffer checks took four minutes to stabilize, against a normal 30 seconds.
A spare electrode in the same process water responded quickly and read steady near 7.0.
Alkali dosing bursts lined up with the slow electrode delayed readings, not with real load changes.
Installing the spare electrode in a trial steadied both pH and dosing within a day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Influent pH truly swings and the loop is responding correctly
A slow, aged pH electrode makes the control loop chase late readings and dose in bursts
The alkali pump is oversized and cannot dose gently
The basin is too poorly mixed for pH control

inference.explanation: The spare electrode in the same water reads steady, contradicting real swings and mixing. Dosing follows the faulty signal, and the swap trial isolates the electrode.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Electrode buffer response test paired with the spare electrode trial
Influent pH trend for the period
Alkali pump sizing record

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: pH and dosing both steady with the responsive electrode, at the same pump.
clueText.nc-b: Influent pH was steady through the swings.
clueText.nc-c: The pump dosed smoothly under the new electrode.

tasks.prompt: Phosphorus removal failed a week after the alum feed was switched to a new bulk tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The new tank product certificate showed a much weaker alum strength than the product the dose pump was set for.
Dose pump output verified correctly in a bucket check, so volume delivered was as set.
Jar tests with the new product needed nearly double the volume to reach the same phosphorus removal.
Recalculating dose on product strength and resetting the pump in a trial restored effluent phosphorus within days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The dose pump has lost capacity since the tank switch
Influent phosphorus doubled in the same week
The dose setting was never corrected for the weaker new alum product, so active chemical delivered fell
The clarifier is washing chemical floc out at current flows

inference.explanation: The bucket check contradicts pump failure and load and flow are not stated to have changed. Jar tests and the strength based reset isolate product strength.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Dose pump bucket check record
Product strength certificate paired with jar tests and the dose reset trial
Influent phosphorus trend

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Pump output matched its setting.
clueText.nc-b: Removal recovers when dose is set on the new product actual strength.
clueText.nc-c: Influent phosphorus was steady.

tasks.prompt: Ferric dosing for phosphorus worked in the day and failed at night, on an unchanged dose rate setting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Night influent flow fell to a third of daytime flow, but the ferric pump ran at a fixed stroke rate.
Daytime dose per litre was correct, while the fixed rate meant the chemical to flow ratio swung widely across the day.
Effluent phosphorus peaked in the early morning samples, matching the hours of lowest chemical per litre treated.
Pacing the pump to flow in a trial week evened the dose per litre and morning phosphorus fell into range.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Ferric loses strength in the tank overnight
Phosphorus load per litre is higher at night from industry
The night operator turns the feed pump down
A fixed rate chemical feed cannot stay proportional as flow swings, so night hours are under dosed

inference.explanation: Load per litre and pump operation are not stated to have changed, and product strength does not follow a clock. Flow pacing at the same product isolates proportionality.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Ferric strength test record
Influent phosphorus per litre trend
Flow paced dosing trial paired with dose per litre calculation across the day

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Ferric strength tested steady day and night.
clueText.nc-b: Phosphorus per litre was flat across the day.
clueText.nc-c: Morning phosphorus passes once dose per litre is held constant by flow pacing.

tasks.prompt: Polymer aided settling stopped working after a new polymer product was brought in at the same dose.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The new product was an anionic polymer, while the sludge jar tests had always responded to the previous cationic product.
Jar tests with the new product showed no floc growth at any dose tried, while the old product in a paired jar flocculated at once.
Sludge charge testing confirmed the solids carried the opposite charge to what the new product supplies.
Restoring a cationic product in a trial returned settling performance the same week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The replacement polymer has the wrong charge for this sludge, so no dose of it can flocculate the solids
The polymer dose is simply too low and must be raised
The polymer make down water is too hard and ruins every product
The sludge changed so that no polymer can work on it

inference.explanation: Paired jars contradict dose, water, and sludge explanations, the old product worked in the same water on the same sludge. Charge testing explains why.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Paired jar tests of old versus new product with sludge charge result
Polymer dose escalation record
Make down water quality record

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Only the correctly charged product flocculates the sludge, at the original dose.
clueText.nc-b: Raising the new product dose in jars still gave no floc.
clueText.nc-c: Make down water was unchanged and suited the old product.

tasks.prompt: Alkalinity dosing held pH well until nitrification improved, then pH began falling despite the same dose.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Effluent ammonia fell from 8 mg/L to 1 mg/L as nitrification recovered, meaning far more ammonia was being oxidized.
Each mg of ammonia nitrogen oxidized consumes about 7.14 mg of alkalinity as CaCO3, so the recovered nitrification roughly doubled alkalinity demand.
Influent alkalinity was unchanged, and the dose system tested at full output.
Raising the dose to the recalculated demand in a trial held pH steady with nitrification still complete.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The alkali product weakened in storage
Recovered nitrification consumes far more alkalinity, and the old dose no longer covers the demand
The pH probe drifted and pH is actually fine
Influent acidity rose and is consuming the alkali

inference.explanation: Product, probe, and influent checks do not support the distractors, while the stoichiometric demand calculation and the dose trial isolate nitrification demand.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Alkali product strength test
Alkalinity demand recalculation at the new nitrification rate paired with the dose trial
pH probe verification record

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Product strength tested at specification.
clueText.nc-b: pH holds at the recalculated dose with full nitrification maintained.
clueText.nc-c: The probe verified against buffers and grabs.

tasks.prompt: External carbon dosing for denitrification overshot, and effluent BOD rose while nitrate removal barely improved past a point.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated period unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Carbon dose records showed dosing continued at the full rate after influent nitrate load fell by half in a plant upgrade.
Anoxic outlet tests showed unused soluble carbon passing through the zone on most days.
Nitrate removal per unit of carbon fell sharply compared with the pre upgrade period.
Trimming the dose to the measured nitrate load in a trial held nitrate removal and brought effluent BOD back down.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The carbon product is contaminated and adds BOD without feeding denitrifiers
Denitrifiers have washed out and cannot use any carbon
Carbon dose was never trimmed to the lower nitrate load, so excess carbon passes through and raises effluent BOD
The anoxic zone is too cold to use the carbon provided

inference.explanation: Unused carbon at the zone outlet contradicts washout and cold limitation, and removal recovered on the trimmed dose of the same product. Load records explain the overshoot.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Carbon product quality certificate
Anoxic zone temperature record
Carbon dose to nitrate load record paired with the dose trimming trial

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Product quality met its certificate.
clueText.nc-b: Anoxic temperature was in its normal range.
clueText.nc-c: Nitrate removal holds on half the carbon once dose follows load.
